clue.text: Smallest creature heading off behind male one

indicators.note: with its heading off, the word loses its first letter

parts.note: M is the standard abbreviation for male
the Roman numeral for one
a creature is an animal

explanation.surface: A zoologist names the tiniest beast, one trailing behind a male of its kind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Behind' places the headless creature after the male and the one, so it ends the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Minimal means the least possible, a straight synonym for smallest in amount or degree.

clue.text: Made list of times I'd condemned purchasing drug

indicators.note: purchasing means taking something in, so the drug goes inside
condemned buildings are torn down, so these letters are demolished and rebuilt

parts.note: taken as written, apostrophe dropped
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: Someone convicted of buying drugs keeps a record of every occasion.
explanation.definitionFit: To itemise is to set out item by item, so itemised means made into a list.

clue.text: Suggest bully is withholding identity

indicators.note: withholding something keeps it back, so those letters are kept out of the word

parts.note: to bully is to intimidate
ID is the short form of identity, as on an ID card

explanation.surface: A victim hints that the bully is concealing who he really is.
explanation.definitionFit: To intimate is to hint or imply something indirectly, a synonym of suggest.

clue.text: Slanders extremely ambitious individuals acquiring newspaper

indicators.note: the extremes of a word are its two end letters, which are kept

parts.note: the first and last letters of ambitious

indicators.note: acquiring something takes it in, so the paper goes inside

parts.note: individuals are persons
the i is a British national newspaper

explanation.surface: Tabloid reporters on the make defame the people they write about.
explanation.walkthrough: The i is a British daily newspaper, so a newspaper can stand for I.
explanation.definitionFit: Aspersions are damaging remarks about someone's character, as in casting aspersions, so they are slanders.

clue.text: Market square

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a periodic gathering for trade
second meaning: just and even-handed, as in a square deal

explanation.walkthrough: 'Market square' reads as the town centre, but the two words are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: A fair is an event where goods are sold, and fair also means honest and equal, the sense of square.

clue.text: Supporter ready for the cup?

parts.note: surface reading: a football fan prepared for the cup final
setter's reading: a piece of crockery that holds up a teacup

explanation.walkthrough: 'Supporter' and 'cup' suggest football; the supporter is a small dish that literally supports a teacup.
explanation.definitionFit: The small plate set under a teacup physically holds it up, so it is a supporter ready for the cup.

clue.text: PM resigned, hard succeeding a leader of stature

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter, which is all that is kept

parts.note: the first letter of stature
someone who resigned quit
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: A prime minister stepped down, a tough act to follow for a towering leader.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Succeeding' puts the resigned-and-hard pair after the A and S. H. H. Asquith was Liberal Prime Minister 1908 to 1916.
explanation.definitionFit: Asquith led the British government as Prime Minister, so he is an example of a PM.

clue.text: Wine from Italy accomplished artist will imbibe

indicators.note: to imbibe is to drink in, so the country's letter goes inside

parts.note: something accomplished has been made or achieved
RA stands for Royal Academician, an artist
I is the international vehicle code for Italy

explanation.surface: A skilled painter will drink a wine from Italy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wine from Italy' reads as one phrase, but the wine is Portuguese and 'from' just links.
explanation.definitionFit: Madeira is a fortified wine from the Portuguese island of the same name, an example of a wine.

clue.text: Country places retired American and I am touring

indicators.note: touring goes round something, so the reversed letters wrap the other piece
to retire is to go back, so these words are read backwards

parts.note: A is a common abbreviation for American
taken as written
to place something is to lay it

explanation.surface: A traveller lists the destinations he and an American have toured.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Places' looks like a noun but is the verb lays; the reversed A, I and AM split around it.
explanation.definitionFit: Malaysia is a nation in South-East Asia, an example of a country.

clue.text: Nameless pedant gets flustered going on about bureaucracy

parts.note: re is Latin-derived for about, as in a letter heading

indicators.note: someone flustered is thrown into disorder, so these letters are jumbled
without a name means the abbreviation for name is taken out of the next word

parts.note: taken as written, before the N for name goes

explanation.surface: A fussy official without a name loses his cool while complaining about paperwork.
explanation.walkthrough: N is the abbreviation for name. 'Going on' puts the jumbled letters after RE.
explanation.definitionFit: Red tape is the idiom for excessive official rules and form-filling, the heart of bureaucracy.

clue.text: Bar opening outside Croatia's capital

indicators.note: one word stands outside, wrapping round the other piece

parts.note: a prelude is an opening piece or event

indicators.note: a capital is a head letter, so only the first letter is kept

parts.note: the first letter of Croatia

explanation.surface: A tourist finds a bar opening on the outskirts of Zagreb.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bar' suggests a pub; here it is the verb meaning prevent.
explanation.definitionFit: To preclude is to rule out or prevent, which is the verb sense of bar.

clue.text: Star figure, great man abroad under pressure …

indicators.note: in a down clue, under means placed below, so the jumbled letters follow

parts.note: P is the symbol for pressure in physics

indicators.note: abroad can mean astray or all over the place, so these letters are scattered

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A star performer, a great man working overseas, is under strain.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis links this clue to the next in the surface only.
explanation.definitionFit: A pentagram is a five-pointed star drawn with five straight lines, a figure shaped like a star.

clue.text: Switch made by socialist around 2001 when upset

indicators.note: upset in a down sense means turned over, so in this clue the result is read backwards
one piece goes around the number, enclosing it

parts.note: a red is a socialist or communist
2001 in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A light switch installed by a left-winger back in 2001 causes trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: A dimmer is a switch that varies the brightness of a light, so it is a type of switch.

clue.text: Rice, possibly regrown, it's ruined

indicators.note: a ruined thing is wrecked, so these letters are broken up and rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written, apostrophe dropped

explanation.surface: A farmer complains that the rice crop which grew back has failed.
explanation.walkthrough: Rice is not the grain but Tim Rice, the lyricist of Jesus Christ Superstar and Evita; 'possibly' marks him as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: Tim Rice writes lyrics for musicals, an example of a person who writes songs.

clue.text: .. strangely he's almost without energy delivering presidential address

indicators.note: doing something strangely means oddly arranged, so these letters are reordered
almost the whole word means its final letter is dropped

parts.note: taken as written, apostrophe dropped
taken as written, before losing its last letter
E is the symbol for energy in physics

explanation.surface: Oddly, he speaks listlessly when giving a presidential speech.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Address' looks like a speech, but it is the place where the US President lives.
explanation.definitionFit: The White House is the official residence of the US President, so it is literally a presidential address.

clue.text: Barely enough given to borrower

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the Christian fasting season, when people eat sparingly
second meaning: handed over on loan

explanation.walkthrough: The first meaning is playful: the forty days before Easter are traditionally lean, with food rationed to barely enough. The second is the past tense of lend.
explanation.definitionFit: The season of fasting suggests meagre rations, while the past participle of lend describes what goes to a borrower.

clue.text: End of homicide case bringing feelings to mind

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter, so only that is kept

parts.note: the last letter of homicide
the vocative is the grammatical case used to address someone

explanation.surface: The close of a murder trial stirs up strong emotions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Case' points to a court or police case; here it is a grammatical case from Latin.
explanation.definitionFit: Something evocative calls up memories or emotions, which is bringing feelings to mind.

clue.text: Cambridge college space attracting Spanish waiter in Torquay?

parts.note: an em is a printer's space
the hapless Spanish waiter in Fawlty Towers, a sitcom set in a Torquay hotel

explanation.surface: A Cambridge college has room to take on a foreign waiter from a seaside town.
explanation.walkthrough: Torquay is an English seaside resort; Fawlty Towers, the 1970s BBC sitcom set there, featured Manuel, a waiter from Barcelona.
explanation.definitionFit: Emmanuel College is one of the constituent colleges of the University of Cambridge.

clue.text: After acting company departs individual becomes depressed

parts.note: the cast is the company of actors in a production
D is the timetable abbreviation for departs
one's own is individual to oneself

explanation.surface: When the theatre troupe leaves, one actor feels low.
explanation.definitionFit: To be cast down is an old idiom for being dejected, the same feeling as depressed.

clue.text: Keen movement raised call for help needlessly

parts.note: to keen is to wail or cry in grief

indicators.note: in a down clue, raised means lifted upwards, so the word reads bottom to top

parts.note: a flow is a movement, as of water

explanation.surface: An eager movement raised an unnecessary alarm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Keen' reads as eager but is the verb meaning to wail.
explanation.definitionFit: To cry wolf, from Aesop's fable, is to raise false alarms, calling for help when none is needed.

clue.text: Live with disheartened young man, providing support

indicators.note: with its heart removed, the word loses its middle letter

parts.note: to stand something is to tolerate or live with it
a boy is a young man

explanation.surface: A dejected youth, given a roof, finds support in living with someone.
explanation.definitionFit: To stand by someone is to remain loyal and support them in difficulty.

clue.text: Tight-fisted with money? Not entirely

indicators.note: not the entire word, so its final letter is dropped

parts.note: means are money or resources, as in a person of means

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a miser is careful with cash and hears that it is only partly true.
explanation.definitionFit: Mean in British usage describes someone unwilling to spend or share, the same idea as stingy and tight-fisted.

clue.text: Cooking apparatus belonging to heiress, it originates from the east

indicators.note: in an across clue, coming from the east means reading right to left
the letters belong to, and so sit inside, the words that follow

parts.note: the run of letters from the inside of these words

explanation.surface: An heiress owns a fancy oven imported from the Orient.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Originates' seems to tell where the device came from, but it just supplies its first three letters to the hidden run.
explanation.definitionFit: A rotisserie is a rotating spit for roasting meat, a piece of cooking equipment.

clue.text: Opportunity to watch big game, live?

definitions.text: Opportunity to watch big game, live?

parts.words: Opportunity to watch big game, live?
parts.note: surface reading: a ticket to see an important match in the stadium

parts.words: Opportunity to watch big game, live?
parts.note: setter's reading: a trip to observe large wild animals in their habitat

explanation.walkthrough: 'Big game' suggests a cup final; it is the hunting term for large wild animals such as lions and elephants, seen alive.
explanation.definitionFit: An African expedition to view large wild animals in the flesh is literally a chance to see big game live.

clue.text: Signs of love for Scottish football club

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the heart symbols that stand for love
second meaning: Heart of Midlothian, the Edinburgh team

explanation.walkthrough: Heart of Midlothian, an Edinburgh football club, is universally called by this nickname.
explanation.definitionFit: Heart shapes are the conventional emblems of affection, and the same word is the everyday name of an Edinburgh team.

clue.text: Exchanging tips, discover rich renewable energy source

indicators.note: tips are the front ends of words, and these two words swap them with each other

parts.note: to discover is to find
a rich colour or tone is warm

explanation.surface: Swapping advice, people learn of a lucrative green power scheme.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tips' suggests advice, but means the first letters of the two words, which change places.
explanation.definitionFit: A wind farm is a group of wind turbines generating electricity, a renewable energy source.

clue.text: Voiced regret making mixture to thicken soup

indicators.note: voiced means spoken, so the word is judged by how it sounds

parts.note: to regret is to rue, which is said the same way

explanation.surface: A cook apologises for the soup thickener she has just prepared.
explanation.definitionFit: A roux is flour cooked in fat, a base used to thicken sauces and soups.

clue.text: Present cricket side is unfairly exploited

parts.note: to put up a candidate or idea is to present it
the on side is the leg side of the cricket field

explanation.surface: A cricket team is being taken advantage of.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the on side is the half of the field behind the batsman's legs, also called leg side.
explanation.definitionFit: Being put-upon means being taken advantage of or burdened unfairly, matching unfairly exploited.

clue.text: Tree the French planted by stream? Er, not sure

parts.note: la is French for the, feminine
a burn is a Scottish and northern English word for a stream
um is the noise of hesitation

explanation.surface: Someone hesitantly suggests a tree was planted beside a stream by the French.
explanation.walkthrough: A burn is a small stream in Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: Laburnum is a small tree with hanging yellow flowers, an example of a tree.

clue.text: Choose Alan Titchmarsh to introduce DIY product

indicators.note: the phrase before introduces, or presents within itself, the letters that follow

parts.note: the run of letters spanning the end of the first word, the whole second, and the start of the third

explanation.surface: A TV producer picks the gardening presenter to front a home-improvement item.
explanation.walkthrough: Alan Titchmarsh is a British gardening broadcaster; the famous name invites a search for wordplay on Alan, but the letters simply run across the words.
explanation.definitionFit: Sealant is a substance used to fill gaps and make joints watertight, a typical home-improvement material.
